name: Musiri (Muziris)
description: The crown jewel of Roman trade in India, famed for its massive exports of black pepper, malabathrum (cinnamon leaves), and high-quality ivory.

name: Poompuhar (Kaveripoompattinam)
description: A magnificent port city at the mouth of the Kaveri River, described in Sangam literature (Pattinappalai) as a bustling metropolis of international traders.

name: Korkai
description: The legendary center of pearl diving. Celebrated by Greek geographers and Tamil poets alike for the finest pearls in the ancient world.

name: Arikamedu (Poduke)
description: An active manufacturing and shipping hub where Romans established a permanent trading post. Famed for bead-making (glass and semi-precious stones).

name: Berenike
description: The desert gate to the Roman Empire. Cargo from Muziris was unloaded here and carried via camel caravans to the Nile, then shipped to Rome.

name: Kadaram (Kedah Valley)
description: A crucial maritime crossroads in the Malacca Strait. Visited by Chola fleets and merchants trading in tin and exotic spices.

name: Guangzhou (Khanfu)
description: The easternmost destination of ancient Tamil merchant guilds like the *Ayyavole 500*. Trade centered around premium silks, porcelain, and aromatics.
